approval.trigger: None, and not in a good way: there is no approval process because there is no program. This is 'no door to knock on', not GitHub-style 'no approval needed'.

blockers.detail: Exhaustive checking found no developer portal, no API docs, no app registration, no authorization endpoints, and no developer terms. Cricbuzz's Terms describe the service purely as consumer content. The reseller ecosystem exists precisely because no official channel does.
blockers.howToClear: You cannot clear this. Choose an alternative data route (see steps) instead of waiting for a program that does not exist.
blockers.title: No developer program exists

blockers.detail: Cricbuzz's Terms of Use prohibit automated access, crawling, scraping, and data extraction in explicit, repeated language (§4 'Personal Use Only', prohibited-activities list, §12 IP). Marketplace listings named 'Cricbuzz Official APIs' are published by individual third-party sellers, not Cricbuzz, and are built on the activity the Terms prohibit.
blockers.howToClear: Do not build a product on resellers or scraping. The breakage and ToS risk sits entirely with you.
blockers.title: Scraping and reseller APIs violate Cricbuzz's Terms

name: Cricbuzz
nuances: The difficulty rating means 'no path exists', not 'the path is hard'. Every other guide in this library is about navigating a process; this one is about recognizing a dead end early.

Cricbuzz's valuable content (live scores, commentary, stats, news) is accessible with no account at all, per its own Terms §1. The OAuth question dissolves: the scores feed is a content-licensing question, not an authorization question.

Per-user data (followed teams, alert preferences) lives inside Cricbuzz with no export or API. If your agent needs 'alert me about my teams', hold those preferences in your own app and match them against a licensed feed; Cricbuzz never enters the loop.
Listings literally named 'Cricbuzz Official APIs' on marketplaces like RapidAPI are individual third-party sellers. 'Official' in the listing name is marketing, not a Cricbuzz product.
prerequisites: Nothing to prepare: there is nothing to register for. What you need is a decision about which alternative data route fits your product.

steps.detail: Before budgeting anything, confirm the negative: Cricbuzz publishes no developer portal, API documentation, or partner program, and its Terms never contemplate third-party app access. This guide exists so you spend minutes learning that, not days.
steps.title: Accept there is nothing to register

steps.detail: Ask which of these you actually need: (a) live scores/stats/news content, or (b) the user's Cricbuzz account data (followed teams, alerts). (a) is a data-licensing problem. (b) is simply not available, to anyone, at any price we could find.
steps.title: Decide what you actually need

steps.detail: License equivalent cricket data from an independent provider with its own feed: CricketData.org (free tier ~100 hits/day, paid from ~$5.99/mo, third-party-reported) for hobby scale; Roanuz (cricketapi.com, published plans) for fantasy/chatbot products; Sportradar or EntitySport for enterprise. These are legitimate, stable, and do not depend on Cricbuzz at all.
steps.title: License a data provider instead

steps.detail: Integration is API-key auth against the provider's REST endpoints (fixtures, live scores, scorecards). No OAuth flow, no user consent screen, no approval wait. Your agent can implement and test this end to end.
steps.title: Integrate via API key

steps.detail: Store followed teams/players and alert preferences in your own product, and trigger notifications from the licensed feed. Do not design any feature that assumes reading them from Cricbuzz.
steps.title: Hold user preferences yourself

steps.detail: (Optional, low odds) Cricbuzz publishes only generic contact routes (support@cricbuzz.com, grievance@cricbuzz.com, cricbuzz.com/info/contact), none framed as licensing. A 2015 report described a B2B scores business; whether an equivalent exists today is unverified. Treat any outreach as exploratory with no stated timeline.
steps.title: Optionally, ask Cricbuzz directly

tagline: The honest dead end: Cricbuzz has no OAuth app, no public API, and no developer program at any difficulty level. The guide is about what to do instead.

time.active: 0 min with Cricbuzz (no path exists); ~half a day to integrate a licensed data provider
time.total: No Cricbuzz integration is possible; a licensed-provider integration can be live the same day
time.waiting: None, because there is no queue to join
